"""Gated rollout-side timing instrumentation for GUI actor RL.

Purpose: diagnose why rollout wall-clock grows across training (e.g. 40min ->
100min per rollout) by recording, PER TRAJECTORY, how long every phase takes:

    semaphore wait -> env allocate -> env reset -> actor step 0..N
    (generation vs env execution) -> env evaluate -> judge round 0
    -> probe round 0 -> judge round 1 -> ... -> env close

together with WHICH task the trajectory belongs to (rollout_id, sample index,
group index, domain, example_id, instruction) and the final outcome
(status, env score, judge verdict).

Everything is gated by ``gui_timing_log_enable`` (runtime YAML, injected via
--custom-config-path) or the env var ``GUI_TIMING_LOG_ENABLE``. When disabled
every recorder method is a no-op and nothing is written.

Output layout (easy to eyeball, one dir per rollout step)::

    ${GUI_TIMING_LOG_DIR}/                      # default: <GUI_RESULT_DIR>/../logs/rollout_timing
        rollout_0003/
            chrome__abc-uuid__s17.json          # full per-trajectory detail
        rollout_0003.jsonl                      # one line per finished trajectory (streamed)
        rollout_0003_summary.json               # aggregate written when the rollout ends

The recorder is purely wall-clock bookkeeping around existing awaits — it never
changes rollout/judge behavior.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import asyncio
import logging
import os
import re
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from functools import partial
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
_TIMING_WRITER = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix="gui-timing-writer")


class EventLoopLagMonitor:
    """Bounded counters; one monitor per rollout, including failed rollouts."""
    def __init__(self, interval=0.1):
        self.interval = interval
        self.count = self.over_100ms = 0
        self.total = self.maximum = 0.0
        self.task = asyncio.create_task(self._sample())

    async def _sample(self):
        while True:
            start = time.monotonic()
            await asyncio.sleep(self.interval)
            lag = max(0.0, time.monotonic() - start - self.interval)
            self.count += 1
            self.total += lag
            self.maximum = max(self.maximum, lag)
            self.over_100ms += lag >= 0.1

    async def stop(self):
        self.task.cancel()
        try:
            await self.task
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass
        return {"perf/event_loop_lag_mean_s": self.total / max(1, self.count),
                "perf/event_loop_lag_max_s": self.maximum,
                "perf/event_loop_lag_over_100ms": self.over_100ms,
                "perf/event_loop_lag_samples": self.count}


async def start_event_loop_monitor():
    return EventLoopLagMonitor()

# Set by gui_generate_rollout (the --rollout-function-path /
# --eval-function-path wrapper) before samples are generated, so per-sample
# recorders know which rollout step they belong to.
_CURRENT_ROLLOUT_ID: int = -1


def set_current_rollout_id(rollout_id: int) -> None:
    global _CURRENT_ROLLOUT_ID
    _CURRENT_ROLLOUT_ID = int(rollout_id)


def get_current_rollout_id() -> int:
    return _CURRENT_ROLLOUT_ID


def timing_enabled(args: Any) -> bool:
    cfg = getattr(args, "gui_timing_log_enable", None)
    if cfg is not None:
        return bool(cfg)
    return os.getenv("GUI_TIMING_LOG_ENABLE", "0").strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes"}


def timing_log_dir(args: Any) -> Path:
    configured = getattr(args, "gui_timing_log_dir", None) or os.getenv("GUI_TIMING_LOG_DIR", "")
    if configured:
        return Path(str(configured))
    # GUI_RESULT_DIR defaults to <run_dir>/results -> put timing next to it
    # under <run_dir>/logs/rollout_timing so it sits with the other run logs.
    result_dir = Path(os.getenv("GUI_RESULT_DIR", "./results"))
    return result_dir.parent / "logs" / "rollout_timing"


def _safe_tag(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zA-Z._-]+", "_", str(text))[:120]


class SampleTimingRecorder:
    """Per-trajectory wall-clock recorder. All methods no-op when disabled."""

    def __init__(self, args: Any, *, sample_index: Any, group_index: Any,
                 domain: str, example_id: str, instruction: str, evaluation: bool):
        self.enabled = timing_enabled(args)
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        self.base_dir = timing_log_dir(args)
        self.rollout_id = get_current_rollout_id()
        self.sample_index = sample_index
        self.record: dict[str, Any] = {
            "rollout_id": self.rollout_id,
            "sample_index": sample_index,
            "group_index": group_index,
            "domain": domain,
            "example_id": example_id,
            "instruction": instruction,
            "evaluation": evaluation,
            "start_time": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
            "phases": {},          # phase name -> seconds (env_allocate, env_reset, ...)
            "steps": [],           # per actor step: {step, total_s, gen_s, gen_attempts, env_exec_s, num_actions}
            "judge_rounds": [],    # per judge round: {round, judge_s, judge_attempts, probe_s, probe_steps}
        }
        self._t0 = time.monotonic()

    # ── phases ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    @contextmanager
    def phase(self, name: str):
        """Time a named phase (env_allocate / env_reset / env_evaluate / ...)."""
        if not self.enabled:
            yield
            return
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
            self.record["phases"][name] = round(self.record["phases"].get(name, 0.0) + elapsed, 3)

    # ── actor steps ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def start_step(self, step_idx: int) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        self._step = {
            "step": step_idx, "total_s": 0.0, "gen_s": 0.0,
            "gen_attempts": 0, "env_exec_s": 0.0, "num_actions": 0,
            # per-step diagnostics (why did this step go wrong?)
            "finish_type": "",     # sglang finish reason of the ACCEPTED attempt ("length" = truncated thinking)
            "gen_tokens": 0,       # response tokens of the accepted attempt
            "parse_ok": False,     # tool-call parse succeeded within retries
            "actions": [],         # executed action strings (truncated), incl. WAIT/DONE/FAIL markers
            "done": False,
        }
        self._step_t0 = time.monotonic()

    def note_step(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Attach diagnostic key/values to the current step (no-op when disabled)."""
        if not self.enabled or not hasattr(self, "_step"):
            return
        self._step.update(kwargs)

    def note_step_action(self, action: Any) -> None:
        if not self.enabled or not hasattr(self, "_step"):
            return
        self._step["actions"].append(str(action)[:120])

    @contextmanager
    def step_generate(self):
        if not self.enabled:
            yield
            return
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self._step["gen_s"] += time.monotonic() - start
            self._step["gen_attempts"] += 1

    @contextmanager
    def step_env_exec(self):
        if not self.enabled:
            yield
            return
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self._step["env_exec_s"] += time.monotonic() - start
            self._step["num_actions"] += 1

    def end_step(self) -> None:
        if not self.enabled or not hasattr(self, "_step"):
            return
        self._step["total_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - self._step_t0, 3)
        self._step["gen_s"] = round(self._step["gen_s"], 3)
        self._step["env_exec_s"] = round(self._step["env_exec_s"], 3)
        self.record["steps"].append(self._step)
        del self._step

    # ── judge/probe rounds (filled by judge_infer via this list) ─────
    @property
    def judge_rounds(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]] | None:
        return self.record["judge_rounds"] if self.enabled else None

    # ── finalize ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    async def finalize_async(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        # Files live on shared storage. Even one slow mkdir/write used to
        # stall every socket/timeout in the rollout event loop. A single
        # writer preserves JSONL record ordering without concurrent append.
        if self.enabled:
            await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(
                _TIMING_WRITER, partial(
                    self.finalize, **kwargs, _end_time=datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                    _elapsed_s=round(time.monotonic() - self._t0, 3)
                )
            )

    def finalize(self, *, status: str, eval_score: float,
                 judge_status: str | None, judge_used_probe: bool | None,
                 result_dir: str | None = None,
                 reward_score: float | None = None,
                 removed_from_training: bool | None = None,
                 error: str | None = None, retry_attempts: list | None = None,
                 _end_time=None, _elapsed_s=None) -> None:
        """Write the per-sample JSON + append to the per-rollout JSONL."""
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        rec = self.record
        rec["end_time"] = _end_time or datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
        rec["total_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - self._t0, 3) if _elapsed_s is None else _elapsed_s
        # Historical total_s is the final attempt only. Expose prior attempts
        # too, so a recovered reset does not hide minutes of rollout latency.
        rec["retry_attempts"] = list(retry_attempts or [])
        rec["retry_total_s"] = round(sum(r["elapsed_s"] for r in rec["retry_attempts"]), 3)
        rec["total_with_retries_s"] = rec["total_s"] + rec["retry_total_s"]
        rec["status"] = status
        rec["env_score"] = eval_score
        rec["judge_status"] = judge_status
        rec["judge_used_probe"] = judge_used_probe
        rec["reward_score"] = reward_score
        rec["removed_from_training"] = removed_from_training
        rec["error"] = (str(error)[:500] if error else None)
        rec["result_dir"] = result_dir
        rec["num_steps"] = len(rec["steps"])
        rec["gen_total_s"] = round(sum(s["gen_s"] for s in rec["steps"]), 3)
        rec["env_exec_total_s"] = round(sum(s["env_exec_s"] for s in rec["steps"]), 3)
        rec["judge_total_s"] = round(sum(r.get("judge_s", 0.0) for r in rec["judge_rounds"]), 3)
        rec["probe_total_s"] = round(sum(r.get("probe_s", 0.0) for r in rec["judge_rounds"]), 3)
        # trajectory-level diagnostics (each is a "why is acc low?" signal)
        steps = rec["steps"]
        rec["gen_attempts_total"] = sum(s.get("gen_attempts", 0) for s in steps)
        rec["parse_fail_steps"] = sum(1 for s in steps if not s.get("parse_ok", True))
        rec["truncated_steps"] = sum(1 for s in steps if s.get("finish_type") == "length")
        rec["gen_tokens_total"] = sum(s.get("gen_tokens", 0) for s in steps)
        rec["gen_tokens_max"] = max((s.get("gen_tokens", 0) for s in steps), default=0)
        rec["terminated_by"] = _terminated_by(steps, status)

        try:
            rollout_tag = f"rollout_{self.rollout_id:04d}" if self.rollout_id >= 0 else "rollout_unknown"
            detail_dir = self.base_dir / rollout_tag
            detail_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            fname = f"{_safe_tag(rec['domain'])}__{_safe_tag(rec['example_id'])}__s{rec['sample_index']}.json"
            with open(detail_dir / fname, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(rec, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
            with open(self.base_dir / f"{rollout_tag}.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            # Global per-task history: one compact line per trajectory, ALL
            # rollouts in one file — grep a task id to see its whole training
            # history (env/judge score over time) at a glance.
            compact = {k: rec.get(k) for k in (
                "rollout_id", "sample_index", "group_index", "domain", "example_id",
                "status", "env_score", "judge_status", "reward_score",
                "removed_from_training", "judge_used_probe", "num_steps",
                "terminated_by", "truncated_steps", "parse_fail_steps",
                "gen_attempts_total", "gen_tokens_max", "total_s", "retry_total_s", "total_with_retries_s", "end_time", "error",
            )}
            with open(self.base_dir / "task_history.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps(compact, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        except Exception:
            logger.warning("failed to write timing record", exc_info=True)

        logger.info(
            "[GUI-TIMING] rollout=%s sample=%s %s/%s total=%.1fs "
            "(alloc=%.1fs reset=%.1fs gen=%.1fs env_exec=%.1fs eval=%.1fs judge=%.1fs probe=%.1fs close=%.1fs) "
            "steps=%d term=%s trunc=%d parse_fail=%d judge_rounds=%d status=%s judge=%s env_score=%.2f",
            self.rollout_id, rec["sample_index"], rec["domain"], rec["example_id"], rec["total_s"],
            rec["phases"].get("env_allocate", 0.0), rec["phases"].get("env_reset", 0.0),
            rec["gen_total_s"], rec["env_exec_total_s"], rec["phases"].get("env_evaluate", 0.0),
            rec["judge_total_s"], rec["probe_total_s"], rec["phases"].get("env_close", 0.0),
            rec["num_steps"], rec["terminated_by"], rec["truncated_steps"], rec["parse_fail_steps"],
            len(rec["judge_rounds"]), status, judge_status, eval_score,
        )


def _terminated_by(steps: list[dict[str, Any]], status: str) -> str:
    """How did the trajectory end? One of:
    done_marker (model said DONE/FAIL) / env_done / max_steps / repetitive_action / context_exhausted /
    parse_fail (retries exhausted) / abort / unknown."""
    if status == "aborted":
        return "abort"
    if steps:
        last = steps[-1]
        if last.get("stop_reason") in {"repetitive_action", "context_exhausted"}:
            return last["stop_reason"]
        if not last.get("parse_ok", True):
            return "parse_fail"
        actions = last.get("actions") or []
        if any(str(a).strip().upper() in {"DONE", "FAIL"} for a in actions):
            return "done_marker"
        if last.get("done"):
            return "env_done"
    if status == "truncated":
        return "max_steps"
    return status or "unknown"


def write_rollout_summary(args: Any, rollout_id: int) -> None:
    """Aggregate the per-rollout JSONL into rollout_XXXX_summary.json.

    Called by gui_generate_rollout after the rollout finishes. Reads the JSONL
    back so it works regardless of which coroutine wrote each record.
    """
    if not timing_enabled(args):
        return
    base_dir = timing_log_dir(args)
    rollout_tag = f"rollout_{rollout_id:04d}"
    jsonl_path = base_dir / f"{rollout_tag}.jsonl"
    if not jsonl_path.exists():
        return
    try:
        records = [json.loads(line) for line in jsonl_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("failed to read timing jsonl %s", jsonl_path, exc_info=True)
        return
    if not records:
        return

    def _agg(key: str) -> dict[str, float]:
        vals = [float(r.get(key, 0.0) or 0.0) for r in records]
        return {
            "sum": round(sum(vals), 1),
            "mean": round(sum(vals) / len(vals), 1),
            "max": round(max(vals), 1),
        }

    # ── outcome metrics, PER TRAJECTORY (unweighted by dynamic_history fan-out,
    # unlike wandb rollout/acc which averages over child samples) ──
    # NOTE: env_score 0.0 is a legitimate failure score; only None / <0
    # (evaluate() errored, recorded as -1) is excluded. Do not use `or` here.
    def _env_score(r: dict[str, Any]) -> float:
        v = r.get("env_score")
        return -1.0 if v is None else float(v)

    scored = [r for r in records if _env_score(r) >= 0.0]
    env_acc = round(sum(_env_score(r) for r in scored) / len(scored), 4) if scored else None
    judge_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    term_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for r in records:
        judge_counts[str(r.get("judge_status"))] = judge_counts.get(str(r.get("judge_status")), 0) + 1

=== judge_infer.py ===
"""Frozen-judge inference for GUI actor RL — the judge->probe->judge state machine.

This replicates, byte-for-byte in behavior, the judge-scoring loop from
``guirl.slime_custom.custom_generate`` (roughly lines 560–810) — the SAME loop
used while the judge was being TRAINED — with all *training* mechanics dropped
(token accumulation, loss_mask, logprobs, fan-out, multimodal encoding). The
judge here is FROZEN and served on a standalone sglang ``/chat/completions``, so
it produces no gradients; only its verdict matters.

What is aligned to training (do not change without changing slime_custom too):
- prompt = ``[{system: JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {user: build_judge_user_content(...)}]``;
- linear messages list, appended each round (NOT rebuilt every round);
- ``for round_idx in range(max_rounds)`` with the exact stop-condition ORDER;
- history carries only conclusions (``_strip_thinking_for_history``);
- probe on "uncertain" via the rollout master (holo3 harness), whose
  ``latest_criteria`` + ``criteria_images`` feed the next round DIRECTLY;
- parse retry keeps temperature (=1.0); exhaust -> "parse_failure";
- sampling temperature=1.0 / max_tokens=24576 / enable_thinking=true.

Only two things differ from guirl (because we train the actor, not the judge):
reward mapping is actor-semantics (handled by the caller), and the judge is a
frozen HTTP endpoint instead of the training engine.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from typing import Any

from guirl.judge.judge_prompts import (
    JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    JudgeStatus,
    _strip_thinking_for_history,
    build_judge_user_content,
)

from gui_actor_rl.judge_client import JudgeClient, JudgeResult
from gui_actor_rl.probe_client import RolloutMasterProbeRunner

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def run_judge_inference(
    *,
    judge_client: JudgeClient,
    probe_runner: RolloutMasterProbeRunner | None,
    lease_id: str | None,
    fence_token: str | None = None,
    instruction: str,
    trajectory_screenshots: list[str],
    action_history: list[str] | None,
    max_rounds: int = 3,
    history_n: int = 3,
    timing_records: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> JudgeResult:
    """Run the frozen judge's judge->probe->judge loop over one actor trajectory.

    Mirrors ``guirl.slime_custom.custom_generate``'s judge loop (inference only).
    Never raises: probe/network/parse failures degrade to a usable verdict or to
    ``status="parse_failure"`` so the caller can drop the sample from training.

    Must be called while the env ``lease_id`` is still open — the probe steps the
    SAME VM to gather evidence for "uncertain" criteria.

    ``timing_records`` (optional, gated instrumentation): when provided, one dict
    per round is appended: ``{round, judge_s, judge_attempts, judge_status,
    probe_s, probe_steps}``. Pure bookkeeping — never changes behavior.
    """
    if not trajectory_screenshots:
        return JudgeResult(status="parse_failure", error="empty trajectory (no screenshots)")

    # === Unified linear messages list (mirrors slime_custom / evaluation_harness). ===
    # Round 0 user turn: trajectory screenshots + action history, no prev criteria.
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
        {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}]},
    ]
    user_content_r0 = build_judge_user_content(
        task=instruction,
        task_traj_imgs=trajectory_screenshots,
        prev_criteria=None,
        action_history=list(action_history) if action_history else None,
        history_n=history_n,
        criteria_option_screenshot=None,
    )
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_content_r0})

    current_status: JudgeStatus = "uncertain"
    current_criteria: str = ""
    last_response_text: str = ""
    num_rounds = 0
    used_probe = False
    probe_steps = 0

    for round_idx in range(max_rounds):
        num_rounds = round_idx + 1
        round_timing: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        if timing_records is not None:
            round_timing = {"round": round_idx, "judge_s": 0.0, "judge_attempts": 0,
                            "judge_status": "", "probe_s": 0.0, "probe_steps": 0}
            timing_records.append(round_timing)

        # --- judge generate with parse-retry (keeps temperature; -> parse_failure). ---
        _judge_t0 = time.monotonic()
        response_text, current_status, current_criteria, _attempts = await judge_client.chat_parseable(
            messages, round_idx=round_idx
        )
        if round_timing is not None:
            round_timing["judge_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _judge_t0, 3)
            round_timing["judge_attempts"] = _attempts
            round_timing["judge_status"] = current_status
        last_response_text = response_text

        # --- Stop conditions, in the SAME ORDER as slime_custom. ---
        is_last_round = (
            current_status == "parse_failure"
            or current_status != "uncertain"
            or round_idx >= max_rounds - 1
            or lease_id is None
        )

        # Append this round's assistant reply to history BEFORE deciding to stop,
        # with thinking stripped so the next round sees only conclusions (aligned
        # to slime_custom, which also strips history thinking on continuing rounds).
        # On parse_failure there is nothing parseable to carry; skip the append.
        if current_status != "parse_failure":
            messages.append(
                {"role": "assistant", "content": _strip_thinking_for_history(response_text)}
            )

        if is_last_round:
            break

        # --- uncertain + not last round + lease alive + probe available -> probe. ---
        if probe_runner is None:
            # No probe configured: cannot resolve "uncertain"; stop here and let
            # the caller drop the sample (actor-semantics).
            break

        try:
            _probe_t0 = time.monotonic()
            probe_result = await probe_runner.run_probe_round(
                lease_id=lease_id,
                fence_token=fence_token,
                criteria_text=current_criteria,
                task_instruction=instruction,
            )
            if round_timing is not None:
                round_timing["probe_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _probe_t0, 3)
                round_timing["probe_steps"] = int(probe_result.num_steps)
        except Exception as exc:
            if round_timing is not None:
                round_timing["probe_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _probe_t0, 3)
            logger.warning("probe round failed (round %d): %s", round_idx, exc, exc_info=True)
            break

        used_probe = True
        probe_steps += int(probe_result.num_steps)

        # Update criteria from the probe (aligned: probe_result["latest_criteria"]),
        # and feed the probe's evidence screenshots into the next judge round
        # (aligned: probe_result["criteria_images"] as criteria_option_screenshot).
        current_criteria = probe_result.latest_criteria or current_criteria
        evidence = probe_result.criteria_images or None
        user_content_rN = build_judge_user_content(
            task=instruction,
            task_traj_imgs=trajectory_screenshots,
            prev_criteria=current_criteria,
            action_history=None,
            history_n=history_n,
            criteria_option_screenshot=evidence,
        )
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_content_rN})

    return JudgeResult(
        status=current_status,
        criteria_text=current_criteria,
        raw_text=last_response_text,
        attempts=num_rounds,
        num_rounds=num_rounds,
        used_probe=used_probe,
        probe_steps=probe_steps,
    )
=== judge_client.py ===
"""Frozen reward-agent (judge) client for GUI actor RL.

The judge is a trained GUIRL reward agent served on a dedicated (frozen)
sglang instance with an OpenAI-compatible API. Given an actor trajectory
(task instruction + chronological screenshots + action history), it returns
a verdict: success / failure / uncertain / parse_failure.

Prompt building and output parsing are reused verbatim from
``guirl.judge.judge_prompts`` so the judge sees exactly the distribution it
was trained on.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Any

import aiohttp

from guirl.judge.judge_prompts import (
    JudgeStatus,
    ParsedJudgeOutput,
    parse_judge_output,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Thinking judge (24k token output) at high concurrency can exceed 600s.
# sock_read keeps the connection alive; total is the hard ceiling.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=1800, connect=30, sock_read=600)

# Track judge request failures globally (timeout/network/server 5xx) to surface
# in wandb. Reset at module reload (per rollout). Exposed for testing / monitoring.
_judge_request_failed_count = 0


@dataclass
class JudgeResult:
    status: JudgeStatus
    criteria_text: str = ""
    raw_text: str = ""
    attempts: int = 0
    error: str | None = None
    usage: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # judge->probe->judge loop bookkeeping (monitoring only)
    num_rounds: int = 1
    used_probe: bool = False
    probe_steps: int = 0


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _get_judge_semaphore(concurrency: int) -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    return asyncio.Semaphore(max(1, concurrency))


class JudgeClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        base_url: str,
        model_name: str,
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        max_tokens: int = 24576,
        parse_max_retries: int = 3,
        concurrency: int = 16,
        request_max_retries: int = 3,
        enable_thinking: bool = True,
    ):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.model_name = model_name
        self.temperature = float(temperature)
        self.max_tokens = int(max_tokens)
        self.parse_max_retries = max(1, int(parse_max_retries))
        self.request_max_retries = max(1, int(request_max_retries))
        self.concurrency = max(1, int(concurrency))
        self.enable_thinking = bool(enable_thinking)
        self._session: aiohttp.ClientSession | None = None

    @classmethod
    def from_args(cls, args: Any) -> "JudgeClient":
        base_url = getattr(args, "gui_judge_base_url", None) or os.getenv(
            "GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL", "http://host_0:30100/v1"
        )
        model_name = getattr(args, "gui_judge_model_name", None) or os.getenv("GUI_JUDGE_MODEL_NAME", "guirl-judge")
        return cls(
            base_url=str(base_url),
            model_name=str(model_name),
            # Defaults mirror the judge's TRAINING config (guirl 16x2epoch_2node):
            # temperature=1.0, max_tokens=24576, enable_thinking=true. Keeping
            # these aligned matters — the judge is a frozen thinking model and
            # sees a different distribution if sampled differently than trained.
            temperature=float(getattr(args, "gui_judge_temperature", 1.0) or 1.0),
            max_tokens=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_max_tokens", 24576) or 24576),
            parse_max_retries=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_parse_max_retries", 3) or 3),
            concurrency=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_concurrency", 16) or 16),
            enable_thinking=bool(getattr(args, "gui_judge_enable_thinking", True)),
        )

    async def _get_session(self) -> aiohttp.ClientSession:
        if self._session is None or self._session.closed:
            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
        return self._session

    async def _chat(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], temperature: float) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        payload = {
            "model": self.model_name,
            "messages": messages,
            "temperature": temperature,
            "max_tokens": self.max_tokens,
            # Match the judge's TRAINING render exactly: guirl applies the chat
            # template with enable_thinking (see slime_custom._apply_judge_chat_template).
            # sglang's OpenAI endpoint forwards chat_template_kwargs to
            # tokenizer.apply_chat_template, so the frozen judge sees the same
            # thinking-mode prompt it was trained on.
            "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": self.enable_thinking},
        }
        url = f"{self.base_url}/chat/completions"
        session = await self._get_session()
        last_exc: Exception | None = None
        for attempt in range(1, self.request_max_retries + 1):
            try:
                async with session.post(url, json=payload) as resp:
                    data = await resp.json()
                    if resp.status != 200:
                        raise RuntimeError(f"judge HTTP {resp.status}: {data}")
                    text = data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or ""
                    return text, data.get("usage", {}) or {}

                    delay = 2.0 * attempt

                        "judge request attempt %d/%d failed: %s, retrying in %.1fs",
                        attempt,
                        self.request_max_retries,
                        exc,
                        delay,
                    )

        """Raw single chat call, returns response text (no parsing).

        Concurrency is bounded by the shared judge semaphore.

        async with semaphore:

        self,

        does NOT raise temperature.

        is bounded by the shared judge semaphore.

        last_error: Exception | None = None
        last_response = ""

            for attempt in range(1, self.parse_max_retries + 1):
                try:
                    response_text, _usage = await self._chat(messages, temperature=self.temperature)
                except Exception as exc:
                    # Network/server failure is not a parse failure, but there is
                    # nothing usable to train on → degrade to parse_failure.
                    global _judge_request_failed_count
                    _judge_request_failed_count += 1
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge request failed (round %d, attempt %d/%d): %s — sample will be dropped (total_failed=%d)",
                        round_idx,
                        attempt,
                        self.parse_max_retries,
                        exc,
                        _judge_request_failed_count,
                        extra={"judge_request_failed": 1},
                    )
                    return "", "parse_failure", "", attempt

                last_response = response_text
                try:
                    parsed: ParsedJudgeOutput = parse_judge_output(response_text)
                except ValueError as exc:
                    last_error = exc
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge parse failed (round %d, attempt %d/%d): %s",
                        round_idx,
                        attempt,
                        self.parse_max_retries,
                        exc,
                    )
                    continue
                return response_text, parsed.status, parsed.criteria_text, attempt

        logger.warning("judge parse exhausted retries (round %d): %s", round_idx, last_error)
        return last_response, "parse_failure", "", self.parse_max_retries

    async def close_session(self) -> None:
        if self._session and not self._session.closed:
            await self._session.close()
            self._session = None

"""Frozen-judge inference for GUI actor RL — the judge->probe->judge state machine.

This replicates, byte-for-byte in behavior, the judge-scoring loop from
``guirl.slime_custom.custom_generate`` (roughly lines 560–810) — the SAME loop
used while the judge was being TRAINED — with all *training* mechanics dropped
(token accumulation, loss_mask, logprobs, fan-out, multimodal encoding). The
judge here is FROZEN and served on a standalone sglang ``/chat/completions``, so
it produces no gradients; only its verdict matters.

What is aligned to training (do not change without changing slime_custom too):
- prompt = ``[{system: JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {user: build_judge_user_content(...)}]``;
- linear messages list, appended each round (NOT rebuilt every round);
- ``for round_idx in range(max_rounds)`` with the exact stop-condition ORDER;
- history carries only conclusions (``_strip_thinking_for_history``);
- probe on "uncertain" via the rollout master (holo3 harness), whose
  ``latest_criteria`` + ``criteria_images`` feed the next round DIRECTLY;
- parse retry keeps temperature (=1.0); exhaust -> "parse_failure";
- sampling temperature=1.0 / max_tokens=24576 / enable_thinking=true.

Only two things differ from guirl (because we train the actor, not the judge):
reward mapping is actor-semantics (handled by the caller), and the judge is a
frozen HTTP endpoint instead of the training engine.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from typing import Any

from guirl.judge.judge_prompts import (
    JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    JudgeStatus,
    _strip_thinking_for_history,
    build_judge_user_content,
)

from gui_actor_rl.judge_client import JudgeClient, JudgeResult
from gui_actor_rl.probe_client import RolloutMasterProbeRunner

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def run_judge_inference(
    *,
    judge_client: JudgeClient,
    probe_runner: RolloutMasterProbeRunner | None,
    lease_id: str | None,
    fence_token: str | None = None,
    instruction: str,
    trajectory_screenshots: list[str],
    action_history: list[str] | None,
    max_rounds: int = 3,
    history_n: int = 3,
    timing_records: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> JudgeResult:
    """Run the frozen judge's judge->probe->judge loop over one actor trajectory.

    Mirrors ``guirl.slime_custom.custom_generate``'s judge loop (inference only).
    Never raises: probe/network/parse failures degrade to a usable verdict or to
    ``status="parse_failure"`` so the caller can drop the sample from training.

    Must be called while the env ``lease_id`` is still open — the probe steps the
    SAME VM to gather evidence for "uncertain" criteria.

    ``timing_records`` (optional, gated instrumentation): when provided, one dict
    per round is appended: ``{round, judge_s, judge_attempts, judge_status,
    probe_s, probe_steps}``. Pure bookkeeping — never changes behavior.
    """
    if not trajectory_screenshots:
        return JudgeResult(status="parse_failure", error="empty trajectory (no screenshots)")

    # === Unified linear messages list (mirrors slime_custom / evaluation_harness). ===
    # Round 0 user turn: trajectory screenshots + action history, no prev criteria.
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
        {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}]},
    ]
    user_content_r0 = build_judge_user_content(
        task=instruction,
        task_traj_imgs=trajectory_screenshots,
        prev_criteria=None,
        action_history=list(action_history) if action_history else None,
        history_n=history_n,
        criteria_option_screenshot=None,
    )
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_content_r0})

    current_status: JudgeStatus = "uncertain"
    current_criteria: str = ""
    last_response_text: str = ""
    num_rounds = 0
    used_probe = False
    probe_steps = 0

    for round_idx in range(max_rounds):
        num_rounds = round_idx + 1
        round_timing: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        if timing_records is not None:
            round_timing = {"round": round_idx, "judge_s": 0.0, "judge_attempts": 0,
                            "judge_status": "", "probe_s": 0.0, "probe_steps": 0}
            timing_records.append(round_timing)

        # --- judge generate with parse-retry (keeps temperature; -> parse_failure). ---
        _judge_t0 = time.monotonic()
        response_text, current_status, current_criteria, _attempts = await judge_client.chat_parseable(
            messages, round_idx=round_idx
        )
        if round_timing is not None:
            round_timing["judge_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _judge_t0, 3)
            round_timing["judge_attempts"] = _attempts
            round_timing["judge_status"] = current_status
        last_response_text = response_text

        # --- Stop conditions, in the SAME ORDER as slime_custom. ---
        is_last_round = (
            current_status == "parse_failure"
            or current_status != "uncertain"
            or round_idx >= max_rounds - 1
            or lease_id is None
        )

        # Append this round's assistant reply to history BEFORE deciding to stop,
        # with thinking stripped so the next round sees only conclusions (aligned
        # to slime_custom, which also strips history thinking on continuing rounds).
        # On parse_failure there is nothing parseable to carry; skip the append.
        if current_status != "parse_failure":
            messages.append(
                {"role": "assistant", "content": _strip_thinking_for_history(response_text)}
            )

        if is_last_round:
            break

        # --- uncertain + not last round + lease alive + probe available -> probe. ---
        if probe_runner is None:
            # No probe configured: cannot resolve "uncertain"; stop here and let
            # the caller drop the sample (actor-semantics).
            break

        try:
            _probe_t0 = time.monotonic()
            probe_result = await probe_runner.run_probe_round(
                lease_id=lease_id,
                fence_token=fence_token,
                criteria_text=current_criteria,
                task_instruction=instruction,
            )
            if round_timing is not None:
                round_timing["probe_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _probe_t0, 3)
                round_timing["probe_steps"] = int(probe_result.num_steps)
        except Exception as exc:
            if round_timing is not None:
                round_timing["probe_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _probe_t0, 3)
            logger.warning("probe round failed (round %d): %s", round_idx, exc, exc_info=True)
            break

        used_probe = True
        probe_steps += int(probe_result.num_steps)

        # Update criteria from the probe (aligned: probe_result["latest_criteria"]),
        # and feed the probe's evidence screenshots into the next judge round
        # (aligned: probe_result["criteria_images"] as criteria_option_screenshot).
        current_criteria = probe_result.latest_criteria or current_criteria
        evidence = probe_result.criteria_images or None
        user_content_rN = build_judge_user_content(
            task=instruction,
            task_traj_imgs=trajectory_screenshots,
            prev_criteria=current_criteria,
            action_history=None,
            history_n=history_n,
            criteria_option_screenshot=evidence,
        )
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_content_rN})

    return JudgeResult(
        status=current_status,
        criteria_text=current_criteria,
        raw_text=last_response_text,
        attempts=num_rounds,
        num_rounds=num_rounds,
        used_probe=used_probe,
        probe_steps=probe_steps,
    )

"""Frozen reward-agent (judge) client for GUI actor RL.

The judge is a trained GUIRL reward agent served on a dedicated (frozen)
sglang instance with an OpenAI-compatible API. Given an actor trajectory
(task instruction + chronological screenshots + action history), it returns
a verdict: success / failure / uncertain / parse_failure.

Prompt building and output parsing are reused verbatim from
``guirl.judge.judge_prompts`` so the judge sees exactly the distribution it
was trained on.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Any

import aiohttp

from guirl.judge.judge_prompts import (
    JudgeStatus,
    ParsedJudgeOutput,
    parse_judge_output,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Thinking judge (24k token output) at high concurrency can exceed 600s.
# sock_read keeps the connection alive; total is the hard ceiling.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=1800, connect=30, sock_read=600)

# Track judge request failures globally (timeout/network/server 5xx) to surface
# in wandb. Reset at module reload (per rollout). Exposed for testing / monitoring.
_judge_request_failed_count = 0


@dataclass
class JudgeResult:
    status: JudgeStatus
    criteria_text: str = ""
    raw_text: str = ""
    attempts: int = 0
    error: str | None = None
    usage: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # judge->probe->judge loop bookkeeping (monitoring only)
    num_rounds: int = 1
    used_probe: bool = False
    probe_steps: int = 0


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _get_judge_semaphore(concurrency: int) -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    return asyncio.Semaphore(max(1, concurrency))


class JudgeClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        base_url: str,
        model_name: str,
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        max_tokens: int = 24576,
        parse_max_retries: int = 3,
        concurrency: int = 16,
        request_max_retries: int = 3,
        enable_thinking: bool = True,
    ):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.model_name = model_name
        self.temperature = float(temperature)
        self.max_tokens = int(max_tokens)
        self.parse_max_retries = max(1, int(parse_max_retries))
        self.request_max_retries = max(1, int(request_max_retries))
        self.concurrency = max(1, int(concurrency))
        self.enable_thinking = bool(enable_thinking)
        self._session: aiohttp.ClientSession | None = None

    @classmethod
    def from_args(cls, args: Any) -> "JudgeClient":
        base_url = getattr(args, "gui_judge_base_url", None) or os.getenv(
            "GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL", "http://host_0:30100/v1"
        )
        model_name = getattr(args, "gui_judge_model_name", None) or os.getenv("GUI_JUDGE_MODEL_NAME", "guirl-judge")
        return cls(
            base_url=str(base_url),
            model_name=str(model_name),
            # Defaults mirror the judge's TRAINING config (guirl 16x2epoch_2node):
            # temperature=1.0, max_tokens=24576, enable_thinking=true. Keeping
            # these aligned matters — the judge is a frozen thinking model and
            # sees a different distribution if sampled differently than trained.
            temperature=float(getattr(args, "gui_judge_temperature", 1.0) or 1.0),
            max_tokens=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_max_tokens", 24576) or 24576),
            parse_max_retries=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_parse_max_retries", 3) or 3),
            concurrency=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_concurrency", 16) or 16),
            enable_thinking=bool(getattr(args, "gui_judge_enable_thinking", True)),
        )

    async def _get_session(self) -> aiohttp.ClientSession:
        if self._session is None or self._session.closed:
            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
        return self._session

    async def _chat(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], temperature: float) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        payload = {
            "model": self.model_name,
            "messages": messages,
            "temperature": temperature,
            "max_tokens": self.max_tokens,
            # Match the judge's TRAINING render exactly: guirl applies the chat
            # template with enable_thinking (see slime_custom._apply_judge_chat_template).
            # sglang's OpenAI endpoint forwards chat_template_kwargs to
            # tokenizer.apply_chat_template, so the frozen judge sees the same
            # thinking-mode prompt it was trained on.
            "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": self.enable_thinking},
        }
        url = f"{self.base_url}/chat/completions"
        session = await self._get_session()
        last_exc: Exception | None = None
        for attempt in range(1, self.request_max_retries + 1):
            try:
                async with session.post(url, json=payload) as resp:
                    data = await resp.json()
                    if resp.status != 200:
                        raise RuntimeError(f"judge HTTP {resp.status}: {data}")
                    text = data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or ""
                    return text, data.get("usage", {}) or {}
            except Exception as exc:  # network / server hiccups
                last_exc = exc
                if attempt < self.request_max_retries:
                    delay = 2.0 * attempt
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge request attempt %d/%d failed: %s, retrying in %.1fs",
                        attempt,
                        self.request_max_retries,
                        exc,
                        delay,
                    )
                    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
        raise RuntimeError(f"judge request failed after {self.request_max_retries} attempts: {last_exc}")

    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], temperature: float | None = None) -> str:
        """Raw single chat call, returns response text (no parsing).

        Concurrency is bounded by the shared judge semaphore.
        """
        temp = self.temperature if temperature is None else float(temperature)
        semaphore = _get_judge_semaphore(self.concurrency)
        async with semaphore:
            text, _usage = await self._chat(messages, temperature=temp)
        return text

    async def chat_parseable(
        self,
        messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
        *,
        round_idx: int = 0,
    ) -> tuple[str, JudgeStatus, str, int]:
        """Generate a judge response, retrying parse failures at the SAME temperature.

        Aligned byte-for-byte in behavior with
        ``guirl.slime_custom._generate_parseable_judge_response``: re-generate the
        identical ``messages`` until ``parse_judge_output`` succeeds; after
        ``parse_max_retries`` failures the verdict degrades to ``parse_failure``
        (never raises — the caller drops the sample). The retry KEEPS
        ``self.temperature`` (training uses temperature=1.0 on every attempt); it
        does NOT raise temperature.

        Returns ``(response_text, status, criteria_text, attempts)``. Concurrency
        is bounded by the shared judge semaphore.
        """
        semaphore = _get_judge_semaphore(self.concurrency)
        last_error: Exception | None = None
        last_response = ""
        async with semaphore:
            for attempt in range(1, self.parse_max_retries + 1):
                try:
                    response_text, _usage = await self._chat(messages, temperature=self.temperature)
                except Exception as exc:
                    # Network/server failure is not a parse failure, but there is
                    # nothing usable to train on → degrade to parse_failure.
                    global _judge_request_failed_count
                    _judge_request_failed_count += 1
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge request failed (round %d, attempt %d/%d): %s — sample will be dropped (total_failed=%d)",
                        round_idx,
                        attempt,
                        self.parse_max_retries,
                        exc,
                        _judge_request_failed_count,
                        extra={"judge_request_failed": 1},
                    )
                    return "", "parse_failure", "", attempt

                last_response = response_text
                try:
                    parsed: ParsedJudgeOutput = parse_judge_output(response_text)
                except ValueError as exc:
                    last_error = exc
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge parse failed (round %d, attempt %d/%d): %s",
                        round_idx,
                        attempt,
                        self.parse_max_retries,
                        exc,
                    )
                    continue
                return response_text, parsed.status, parsed.criteria_text, attempt

        logger.warning("judge parse exhausted retries (round %d): %s", round_idx, last_error)
        return last_response, "parse_failure", "", self.parse_max_retries

    async def close_session(self) -> None:
        if self._session and not self._session.closed:
            await self._session.close()
            self._session = None

        raw_text=last_response_text,
        attempts=num_rounds,
        num_rounds=num_rounds,

import logging
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Any

from guirl.judge.judge_prompts import (
    JudgeStatus,
    ParsedJudgeOutput,
    parse_judge_output,

# Track judge request failures globally (timeout/network/server 5xx) to surface
# in wandb. Reset at module reload (per rollout). Exposed for testing / monitoring.
_judge_request_failed_count = 0


@dataclass
class JudgeResult:
    status: JudgeStatus
    criteria_text: str = ""
    raw_text: str = ""
    attempts: int = 0
    error: str | None = None

    used_probe: bool = False

@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _get_judge_semaphore(concurrency: int) -> asyncio.Semaphore:
    return asyncio.Semaphore(max(1, concurrency))


class JudgeClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        base_url: str,
        model_name: str,
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        max_tokens: int = 24576,
        parse_max_retries: int = 3,
        concurrency: int = 16,
        request_max_retries: int = 3,
        enable_thinking: bool = True,
    ):

        self.max_tokens = int(max_tokens)
        self.parse_max_retries = max(1, int(parse_max_retries))
        self.request_max_retries = max(1, int(request_max_retries))

            "GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL", "http://host_0:30100/v1"

        return cls(
            base_url=str(base_url),
            model_name=str(model_name),
            # Defaults mirror the judge's TRAINING config (guirl 16x2epoch_2node):
            # temperature=1.0, max_tokens=24576, enable_thinking=true. Keeping
            # these aligned matters — the judge is a frozen thinking model and
            # sees a different distribution if sampled differently than trained.
            temperature=float(getattr(args, "gui_judge_temperature", 1.0) or 1.0),
            max_tokens=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_max_tokens", 24576) or 24576),
            parse_max_retries=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_parse_max_retries", 3) or 3),
            concurrency=int(getattr(args, "gui_judge_concurrency", 16) or 16),
            enable_thinking=bool(getattr(args, "gui_judge_enable_thinking", True)),
        )

        if self._session is None or self._session.closed:
            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
        return self._session

        payload = {
            "model": self.model_name,
            "messages": messages,
            "temperature": temperature,

            # template with enable_thinking (see slime_custom._apply_judge_chat_template).
            # sglang's OpenAI endpoint forwards chat_template_kwargs to
            # tokenizer.apply_chat_template, so the frozen judge sees the same
            # thinking-mode prompt it was trained on.
            "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": self.enable_thinking},
        }

        session = await self._get_session()
        last_exc: Exception | None = None

                    data = await resp.json()
                    if resp.status != 200:
                        raise RuntimeError(f"judge HTTP {resp.status}: {data}")

                    return text, data.get("usage", {}) or {}

                last_exc = exc
                if attempt < self.request_max_retries:
                    delay = 2.0 * attempt
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge request attempt %d/%d failed: %s, retrying in %.1fs",
                        attempt,
                        self.request_max_retries,
                        exc,
                        delay,
                    )
                    await asyncio.sleep(delay)

    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], temperature: float | None = None) -> str:
        """Raw single chat call, returns response text (no parsing).

        Concurrency is bounded by the shared judge semaphore.
        """
        temp = self.temperature if temperature is None else float(temperature)
        semaphore = _get_judge_semaphore(self.concurrency)
        async with semaphore:
            text, _usage = await self._chat(messages, temperature=temp)
        return text

    async def chat_parseable(
        self,
        messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
        *,
        round_idx: int = 0,
    ) -> tuple[str, JudgeStatus, str, int]:
        """Generate a judge response, retrying parse failures at the SAME temperature.

        Aligned byte-for-byte in behavior with
        ``guirl.slime_custom._generate_parseable_judge_response``: re-generate the
        identical ``messages`` until ``parse_judge_output`` succeeds; after
        ``parse_max_retries`` failures the verdict degrades to ``parse_failure``
        (never raises — the caller drops the sample). The retry KEEPS
        ``self.temperature`` (training uses temperature=1.0 on every attempt); it
        does NOT raise temperature.

        Returns ``(response_text, status, criteria_text, attempts)``. Concurrency
        is bounded by the shared judge semaphore.
        """
        semaphore = _get_judge_semaphore(self.concurrency)
        last_error: Exception | None = None
        last_response = ""
        async with semaphore:
            for attempt in range(1, self.parse_max_retries + 1):
                try:
                    response_text, _usage = await self._chat(messages, temperature=self.temperature)
                except Exception as exc:
                    # Network/server failure is not a parse failure, but there is
                    # nothing usable to train on → degrade to parse_failure.
                    global _judge_request_failed_count
                    _judge_request_failed_count += 1
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge request failed (round %d, attempt %d/%d): %s — sample will be dropped (total_failed=%d)",
                        round_idx,
                        attempt,
                        self.parse_max_retries,
                        exc,
                        _judge_request_failed_count,
                        extra={"judge_request_failed": 1},
                    )
                    return "", "parse_failure", "", attempt

                last_response = response_text
                try:
                    parsed: ParsedJudgeOutput = parse_judge_output(response_text)
                except ValueError as exc:
                    last_error = exc
                    logger.warning(
                        "judge parse failed (round %d, attempt %d/%d): %s",
                        round_idx,
                        attempt,
                        self.parse_max_retries,
                        exc,
                    )
                    continue
                return response_text, parsed.status, parsed.criteria_text, attempt

        logger.warning("judge parse exhausted retries (round %d): %s", round_idx, last_error)
        return last_response, "parse_failure", "", self.parse_max_retries

    async def close_session(self) -> None:
        if self._session and not self._session.closed:
            await self._session.close()
            self._session = None

"""Frozen-judge inference for GUI actor RL — the judge->probe->judge state machine.

This replicates, byte-for-byte in behavior, the judge-scoring loop from
``guirl.slime_custom.custom_generate`` (roughly lines 560–810) — the SAME loop
used while the judge was being TRAINED — with all *training* mechanics dropped
(token accumulation, loss_mask, logprobs, fan-out, multimodal encoding). The
judge here is FROZEN and served on a standalone sglang ``/chat/completions``, so
it produces no gradients; only its verdict matters.

What is aligned to training (do not change without changing slime_custom too):
- prompt = ``[{system: JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {user: build_judge_user_content(...)}]``;
- linear messages list, appended each round (NOT rebuilt every round);
- ``for round_idx in range(max_rounds)`` with the exact stop-condition ORDER;
- history carries only conclusions (``_strip_thinking_for_history``);
- probe on "uncertain" via the rollout master (holo3 harness), whose
  ``latest_criteria`` + ``criteria_images`` feed the next round DIRECTLY;
- parse retry keeps temperature (=1.0); exhaust -> "parse_failure";
- sampling temperature=1.0 / max_tokens=24576 / enable_thinking=true.

Only two things differ from guirl (because we train the actor, not the judge):
reward mapping is actor-semantics (handled by the caller), and the judge is a
frozen HTTP endpoint instead of the training engine.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from typing import Any

from guirl.judge.judge_prompts import (
    JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    JudgeStatus,
    _strip_thinking_for_history,
    build_judge_user_content,
)

from gui_actor_rl.judge_client import JudgeClient, JudgeResult
from gui_actor_rl.probe_client import RolloutMasterProbeRunner

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def run_judge_inference(
    *,
    judge_client: JudgeClient,
    probe_runner: RolloutMasterProbeRunner | None,
    lease_id: str | None,
    fence_token: str | None = None,
    instruction: str,
    trajectory_screenshots: list[str],
    action_history: list[str] | None,
    max_rounds: int = 3,
    history_n: int = 3,
    timing_records: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> JudgeResult:
    """Run the frozen judge's judge->probe->judge loop over one actor trajectory.

    Mirrors ``guirl.slime_custom.custom_generate``'s judge loop (inference only).
    Never raises: probe/network/parse failures degrade to a usable verdict or to
    ``status="parse_failure"`` so the caller can drop the sample from training.

    Must be called while the env ``lease_id`` is still open — the probe steps the
    SAME VM to gather evidence for "uncertain" criteria.

    ``timing_records`` (optional, gated instrumentation): when provided, one dict
    per round is appended: ``{round, judge_s, judge_attempts, judge_status,
    probe_s, probe_steps}``. Pure bookkeeping — never changes behavior.
    """
    if not trajectory_screenshots:
        return JudgeResult(status="parse_failure", error="empty trajectory (no screenshots)")

    # === Unified linear messages list (mirrors slime_custom / evaluation_harness). ===
    # Round 0 user turn: trajectory screenshots + action history, no prev criteria.
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
        {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}]},
    ]
    user_content_r0 = build_judge_user_content(
        task=instruction,
        task_traj_imgs=trajectory_screenshots,
        prev_criteria=None,
        action_history=list(action_history) if action_history else None,
        history_n=history_n,
        criteria_option_screenshot=None,
    )
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_content_r0})

    current_status: JudgeStatus = "uncertain"
    current_criteria: str = ""
    last_response_text: str = ""
    num_rounds = 0
    used_probe = False
    probe_steps = 0

    for round_idx in range(max_rounds):
        num_rounds = round_idx + 1
        round_timing: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        if timing_records is not None:
            round_timing = {"round": round_idx, "judge_s": 0.0, "judge_attempts": 0,
                            "judge_status": "", "probe_s": 0.0, "probe_steps": 0}
            timing_records.append(round_timing)

        # --- judge generate with parse-retry (keeps temperature; -> parse_failure). ---
        _judge_t0 = time.monotonic()
        response_text, current_status, current_criteria, _attempts = await judge_client.chat_parseable(
            messages, round_idx=round_idx
        )
        if round_timing is not None:
            round_timing["judge_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _judge_t0, 3)
            round_timing["judge_attempts"] = _attempts
            round_timing["judge_status"] = current_status
        last_response_text = response_text

        # --- Stop conditions, in the SAME ORDER as slime_custom. ---
        is_last_round = (
            current_status == "parse_failure"
            or current_status != "uncertain"
            or round_idx >= max_rounds - 1
            or lease_id is None
        )

        # Append this round's assistant reply to history BEFORE deciding to stop,
        # with thinking stripped so the next round sees only conclusions (aligned
        # to slime_custom, which also strips history thinking on continuing rounds).
        # On parse_failure there is nothing parseable to carry; skip the append.
        if current_status != "parse_failure":
            messages.append(
                {"role": "assistant", "content": _strip_thinking_for_history(response_text)}
            )

        if is_last_round:
            break

        # --- uncertain + not last round + lease alive + probe available -> probe. ---
        if probe_runner is None:
            # No probe configured: cannot resolve "uncertain"; stop here and let
            # the caller drop the sample (actor-semantics).
            break

        try:
            _probe_t0 = time.monotonic()
            probe_result = await probe_runner.run_probe_round(
                lease_id=lease_id,
                fence_token=fence_token,
                criteria_text=current_criteria,
                task_instruction=instruction,
            )
            if round_timing is not None:
                round_timing["probe_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _probe_t0, 3)
                round_timing["probe_steps"] = int(probe_result.num_steps)
        except Exception as exc:
            if round_timing is not None:
                round_timing["probe_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - _probe_t0, 3)
            logger.warning("probe round failed (round %d): %s", round_idx, exc, exc_info=True)
            break

        used_probe = True
        probe_steps += int(probe_result.num_steps)

        # Update criteria from the probe (aligned: probe_result["latest_criteria"]),
        # and feed the probe's evidence screenshots into the next judge round
        # (aligned: probe_result["criteria_images"] as criteria_option_screenshot).
        current_criteria = probe_result.latest_criteria or current_criteria
        evidence = probe_result.criteria_images or None
        user_content_rN = build_judge_user_content(
            task=instruction,
            task_traj_imgs=trajectory_screenshots,
            prev_criteria=current_criteria,
            action_history=None,
            history_n=history_n,
            criteria_option_screenshot=evidence,
        )
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_content_rN})

    return JudgeResult(
        status=current_status,
        criteria_text=current_criteria,
        raw_text=last_response_text,
        attempts=num_rounds,
        num_rounds=num_rounds,
        used_probe=used_probe,
        probe_steps=probe_steps,
    )

=== lines 1-60 ===
"""GUI actor RL rollout with a frozen reward-agent (judge) as the reward.

Adapted from OpenClaw-RL/gui-rl ``generate_with_gui.py``:
- env access goes through guirl's env_service (env master :9900, docker VMs)
  via :class:`gui_actor_rl.env_client.ActorEnvClient`;
- the PRM (process reward model) path is removed entirely;
- the training reward comes from the frozen judge (reward agent) instead of
  the environment's rule-based ``evaluate()``:
    * judge says "success"  -> reward +1.0
    * judge says "failure"  -> reward 0.0
    * "uncertain" / "parse_failure" -> sample is DROPPED from training
      (``remove_sample=True``);
- the rule-based env score is still computed and logged to

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GUI Actor RL — reward services (frozen judge replicas + holo3 probe) on dedicated GPUs.
#
# Started from the *worker* rank of the training job, after Ray and the env workers,
# on the GPUs that are NOT handed to Ray. It brings up:
#
#   judge-0..N-1   sglang, tp=1 each, one GPU each   ─┐
#                                                     ├─ sglang_router → JUDGE_PORT
#   probe          holo3 35B-A3B, tp=PROBE_TP          (exposed on PROBE_PORT, used directly)
#
# On success it writes ${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/reward_services.env with
#
#   GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://host_0:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1
#   GUI_JUDGE_MODEL_NAME=...
#   GUI_PROBE_BASE_URL=http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}/v1
#   GUI_PROBE_MODEL_NAME=...
#   GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=true|false
#
# Usage:
#   start_reward_services.sh start|stop|status|logs [worker-index|router|probe]
#
# Everything is env-overridable; see the config block below.

set -euo pipefail

ACTION="${1:-start}"
LOGSEL="${2:-}"

PYTHON_BIN="${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}"
REWARD_LOG_DIR="${REWARD_LOG_DIR:-/tmp/gui_reward_services}"
# Host written into reward_services.env. Set to the node IP when the trainer runs
# on a different rank than the services (host_0 only works same-pod).
REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST="${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST:-host_0}"
mkdir -p "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}"

# ── judge ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGE_MODEL_PATH="${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH:-${JUDGE_HF_CHECKPOINT:-/workspace/assets/judge-checkpoint/rollout_17}}"
JUDGE_SERVED_NAME="${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME:-guirl-judge}"
# ";"-separated GPU ids, one replica per entry (tp=1)
JUDGE_GPU_LIST="${JUDGE_GPU_LIST:-4;5}"
JUDGE_WORKER_PORT="${JUDGE_WORKER_PORT:-31101}"   # first worker; +i per replica
JUDGE_PORT="${JUDGE_PORT:-31100}"                 # router
JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION="${JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION:-0.60}"
JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT="${JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT:-1800}"
JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY="${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY:-round_robin}"

# ── probe (holo3 35B-A3B) ──────────────────────────────────────────
PROBE_ENABLE="${PROBE_ENABLE:-1}"
PROBE_MODEL_PATH="${PROBE_MODEL_PATH:-/workspace/local/models/Holo-3.1-35B-A3B}"
PROBE_SERVED_NAME="${PROBE_SERVED_NAME:-holo3-1-35b-a3b}"
PROBE_GPUS="${PROBE_GPUS:-6,7}"                   # comma-separated, tp=PROBE_TP
PROBE_TP="${PROBE_TP:-2}"
PROBE_PORT="${PROBE_PORT:-31200}"
PROBE_BACKEND="${PROBE_BACKEND:-sglang}"          # sglang | vllm
PROBE_MEM_FRACTION="${PROBE_MEM_FRACTION:-0.65}"
# Mirrors external/pkgs/run_agentplat/scripts/start_holo31_35b_sglang.sh (the known-good
# Holo-3.1-35B-A3B recipe): qwen3 reasoning parser keeps <think> out of `content`, which
# the probe's JSON-schema parser depends on.
PROBE_REASONING_PARSER="${PROBE_REASONING_PARSER:-qwen3}"
PROBE_DTYPE="${PROBE_DTYPE:-bfloat16}"
PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS="${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS:-64}"
PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND="${PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND:-flashinfer}"
PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT="${PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT:-3600}"
# 1 = abort if the probe cannot start, 0 = warn and continue with probe disabled
PROBE_REQUIRED="${PROBE_REQUIRED:-0}"

# Keep the allocator from failing on fragmentation under multimodal prefill spikes.
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="${PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF:-expandable_segments:True}"

IFS=';' read -r -a JUDGE_GPUS <<< "${JUDGE_GPU_LIST}"
NUM_JUDGE=${#JUDGE_GPUS[@]}

judge_pidfile() { echo "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-$1.pid"; }
judge_log()     { echo "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-$1.log"; }
judge_url()     { echo "http://host_0:$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT + $1 ))"; }

ROUTER_LOG="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-router.log"
PROBE_PIDFILE="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/probe.pid"
PROBE_LOG="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/probe.log"
ENVFILE="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/reward_services.env"

usage() {

  local url="$1" pidfile="$2" timeout="$3" label="$4" log="$5"
  local deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + timeout ))
  printf '[%s] waiting for %s ' "${label}" "${url}"
  while true; do
    if curl -sf "${url}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo " ready"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]] && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${pidfile}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "[${label}] ERROR: process died — see ${log}" >&2
      tail -40 "${log}" >&2 || true
      return 1
    fi
    if (( $(date +%s) > deadline )); then
      echo ""
      echo "[${label}] ERROR: not ready within ${timeout}s — see ${log}" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    printf '.'
    sleep 5
  done
}

start_judge_replica() {
  local i="$1" gpu="$2" port="$3"
  local pidfile; pidfile=$(judge_pidfile "$i")
  local log;     log=$(judge_log "$i")
  if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${pidfile}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "[judge-$i] already running (pid $(cat "${pidfile}")) on GPU ${gpu}:${port}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "[judge-$i] starting — GPU ${gpu}, port ${port}"
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${gpu}" "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path "${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}" \
    --served-model-name "${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}" \
    --host host_1 \
    --port "${port}" \
    --tp-size 1 \
    --mem-fraction-static "${JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION}" \
    > "${log}" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "${pidfile}"
}

start_probe() {
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" != "1" ]]; then
    echo "[probe] disabled (PROBE_ENABLE=${PROBE_ENABLE})"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ ! -d "${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" ]]; then
    echo "[probe] ERROR: model path missing: ${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" >&2
    [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]] && return 1
    PROBE_ENABLE=0
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "[probe] already running (pid $(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")) on GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "[probe] starting — GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS} (tp=${PROBE_TP}), port ${PROBE_PORT}, backend ${PROBE_BACKEND}"
  case "${PROBE_BACKEND}" in
    sglang)
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${PROBE_GPUS}" "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path "${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" \
        --served-model-name "${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${PROBE_PORT}" \
        --tp-size "${PROBE_TP}" \
        --mem-fraction-static "${PROBE_MEM_FRACTION}" \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --dtype "${PROBE_DTYPE}" \
        --max-running-requests "${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS}" \
        --attention-backend "${PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND}" \
        --reasoning-parser "${PROBE_REASONING_PARSER}" \
        > "${PROBE_LOG}" 2>&1 &
      ;;
    vllm)
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${PROBE_GPUS}" "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
        --model "${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" \
        --served-model-name "${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${PROBE_PORT}" \
        --tensor-parallel-size "${PROBE_TP}" \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --dtype "${PROBE_DTYPE}" \
        --max-num-seqs "${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS}" \
        --reasoning-parser holo2 \
        > "${PROBE_LOG}" 2>&1 &
      ;;
    *)
      echo "[probe] ERROR: unknown PROBE_BACKEND=${PROBE_BACKEND}" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  echo $! > "${PROBE_PIDFILE}"
}

write_envfile() {
  local probe_enabled="false"
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]] && [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] \
     && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    probe_enabled="true"
  fi
  cat > "${ENVFILE}" <<EOF
# generated by start_reward_services.sh at $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
export GUI_REWARD_SOURCE=judge
export GUI_JUDGE_EXTERNAL=1
export GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1
export GUI_JUDGE_MODEL_NAME=${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}
export GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=${probe_enabled}
export GUI_PROBE_BASE_URL=http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${PROBE_PORT}/v1
export GUI_PROBE_MODEL_NAME=${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}
EOF
  echo "wrote ${ENVFILE}"
  cat "${ENVFILE}"
}

do_start() {
  if [[ ! -d "${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: JUDGE_MODEL_PATH not found: ${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "=== reward services (judge replicas=${NUM_JUDGE}, probe=${PROBE_ENABLE}) ==="
  echo "  judge model:  ${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}"
  echo "  probe model:  ${PROBE_MODEL_PATH} (tp=${PROBE_TP}, GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS})"

  local i gpu port
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
    gpu="${JUDGE_GPUS[$i]}"
    port=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT + i ))
    start_judge_replica "${i}" "${gpu}" "${port}"
  done

  # probe starts in the background; judge readiness is the critical path
  start_probe || { echo "[probe] failed to start" >&2; exit 1; }

  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
    wait_http "$(judge_url "$i")" "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" "${JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT}" "judge-$i" "$(judge_log "$i")"
  done

  if (( NUM_JUDGE > 1 )); then
    if [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[router] already running (pid $(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}"))"
    else
      local worker_urls=()
      for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
        worker_urls+=("--worker-urls" "$(judge_url "$i")")
      done
      echo "[router] :${JUDGE_PORT} → ${NUM_JUDGE} workers (${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY})"
      "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang_router.launch_router \
        "${worker_urls[@]}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${JUDGE_PORT}" \
        --policy "${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY}" \
        > "${ROUTER_LOG}" 2>&1 &
      echo $! > "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}"
      wait_http "http://host_0:${JUDGE_PORT}" "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" 300 "router" "${ROUTER_LOG}"
    fi
  else
    echo "[router] single judge replica — exposing :${JUDGE_PORT} directly is unnecessary"
    # keep the contract stable: point the env file at the single worker port
    JUDGE_PORT=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT ))
  fi

  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    if wait_http "http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}" "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" "${PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT}" "probe" "${PROBE_LOG}"; then
      :
    else
      if [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]]; then
        echo "[probe] required but not ready — aborting" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "[probe] WARNING: probe not ready; continuing with GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=false" >&2
      PROBE_ENABLE=0
    fi
  fi

  write_envfile
  echo ""
  echo "============================================================"
  echo " reward services ready"
  echo "   judge : http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1  (${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}, ${NUM_JUDGE} replica(s))"
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    echo "   probe : http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${PROBE_PORT}/v1  (${PROBE_SERVED_NAME})"
  else
    echo "   probe : DISABLED"
  fi
  echo "============================================================"
}

kill_pidfile() {
  local pidfile="$1" label="$2"
  if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]]; then
    local pid; pid=$(cat "${pidfile}")
    if kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "stopping ${label} (pid ${pid})"
      kill "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
      for _ in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 1; done
      kill -9 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    rm -f "${pidfile}"
  fi
}

do_stop() {
  local i
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do kill_pidfile "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" "judge-$i"; done
  kill_pidfile "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" "judge-router"
  kill_pidfile "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" "probe"
  rm -f "${ENVFILE}"
  echo "all reward services stopped"
}

do_status() {
  local i port
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
    port=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT + i ))
    if [[ -f "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "$(judge_pidfile "$i")")" 2>/dev/null; then
      local h; h=$(curl -sf "http://host_0:${port}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo healthy || echo starting)
      echo "  judge-$i [GPU ${JUDGE_GPUS[$i]}]: running — :${port} (${h})"
    else
      echo "  judge-$i: NOT running"
    fi
  done
  if [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "  router: running — :${JUDGE_PORT}"
  else
    echo "  router: NOT running"
  fi
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    if [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      local h; h=$(curl -sf "http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo healthy || echo starting)
      echo "  probe [GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS}]: running — :${PROBE_PORT} (${h})"
    else
      echo "  probe: NOT running"
    fi
  else
    echo "  probe: disabled"
  fi
}

# Stay in the foreground so the training launcher (which aborts on any non-trainer
# child exiting, even with rc=0) keeps us alive for the whole run.
do_supervise() {
  local rc=0
  do_start || rc=$?
  if (( rc != 0 )); then
    echo "[supervise] startup failed (rc=${rc}); not supervising" >&2
    exit "${rc}"
  fi
  trap 'echo "[supervise] stopping reward services"; do_stop; exit 0' TERM INT
  echo "[supervise] entered supervision loop"
  local dead_streak=0
  while true; do
    sleep 30
    local judge_down=0
    local i
    for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
      if [[ -f "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" ]] && ! kill -0 "$(cat "$(judge_pidfile "$i")")" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "[supervise] ERROR: judge-$i died" >&2
        judge_down=1
      fi
    done
    if (( NUM_JUDGE > 1 )) && [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] \
       && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[supervise] ERROR: judge router died" >&2
      judge_down=1
    fi
    if (( judge_down )); then
      dead_streak=$(( dead_streak + 1 ))
      if (( dead_streak >= 2 )); then
        echo "[supervise] judge tier is down; aborting the run" >&2
        do_stop
        exit 1
      fi
    else
      dead_streak=0
    fi
    if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]] && [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] \
       && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[supervise] WARNING: probe died — uncertain verdicts will be dropped" >&2
      if [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]]; then do_stop; exit 1; fi
    fi
  done
}

do_logs() {
  case "${LOGSEL}" in
    probe)  tail -n 200 -f "${PROBE_LOG}" ;;
    router) tail -n 200 -f "${ROUTER_LOG}" ;;
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") logs [0-$((NUM_JUDGE-1))|router|probe]" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *)      tail -n 200 -f "$(judge_log "${LOGSEL}")" ;;
  esac
}

case "${ACTION}" in
  start)  do_start ;;
  stop)   do_stop ;;
  restart) do_stop; sleep 3; do_start ;;
  supervise) do_supervise ;;
  status) do_status ;;
  logs)   do_logs ;;
  *) usage; exit 1 ;;
esac
