      echo "[router] :${JUDGE_PORT} → ${NUM_JUDGE} workers (${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY})"
      "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang_router.launch_router \
        "${worker_urls[@]}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${JUDGE_PORT}" \
        --policy "${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY}" \
        > "${ROUTER_LOG}" 2>&1 &
      echo $! > "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}"
      wait_http "http://host_0:${JUDGE_PORT}" "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" 300 "router" "${ROUTER_LOG}"
    fi
  else
    echo "[router] single judge replica — exposing :${JUDGE_PORT} directly is unnecessary"
    # keep the contract stable: point the env file at the single worker port
    JUDGE_PORT=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT ))
  fi

  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    if wait_http "http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}" "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" "${PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT}" "probe" "${PROBE_LOG}"; then
      :
    else
      if [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]]; then
        echo "[probe] required but not ready — aborting" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "[probe] WARNING: probe not ready; continuing with GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=false" >&2
      PROBE_ENABLE=0
    fi
  fi

  write_envfile
  echo ""
  echo "============================================================"
  echo " reward services ready"
  echo "   judge : http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1  (${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}, ${NUM_JUDGE} replica(s))"
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    echo "   probe : http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${PROBE_PORT}/v1  (${PROBE_SERVED_NAME})"
  else
    echo "   probe : DISABLED"
  fi
  echo "============================================================"
}

kill_pidfile() {
  local pidfile="$1" label="$2"
  if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]]; then
    local pid; pid=$(cat "${pidfile}")
    if kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "stopping ${label} (pid ${pid})"
      kill "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
      for _ in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 1; done
      kill -9 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    rm -f "${pidfile}"
  fi
}

do_stop() {
  local i
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do kill_pidfile "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" "judge-$i"; done
  kill_pidfile "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" "judge-router"
  kill_pidfile "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" "probe"
  rm -f "${ENVFILE}"
  echo "all reward services stopped"
}

do_status() {
  local i port
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
    port=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT + i ))
    if [[ -f "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "$(judge_pidfile "$i")")" 2>/dev/null; then
      local h; h=$(curl -sf "http://host_0:${port}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo healthy || echo starting)
      echo "  judge-$i [GPU ${JUDGE_GPUS[$i]}]: running — :${port} (${h})"
    else
      echo "  judge-$i: NOT running"
    fi
  done
  if [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "  router: running — :${JUDGE_PORT}"
  else
    echo "  router: NOT running"
  fi
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    if [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      local h; h=$(curl -sf "http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo healthy || echo starting)
      echo "  probe [GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS}]: running — :${PROBE_PORT} (${h})"
    else
      echo "  probe: NOT running"
    fi
  else
    echo "  probe: disabled"
  fi
}

# Stay in the foreground so the training launcher (which aborts on any non-trainer
# child exiting, even with rc=0) keeps us alive for the whole run.
do_supervise() {
  local rc=0
  do_start || rc=$?
  if (( rc != 0 )); then
    echo "[supervise] startup failed (rc=${rc}); not supervising" >&2
    exit "${rc}"
  fi
  trap 'echo "[supervise] stopping reward services"; do_stop; exit 0' TERM INT
  echo "[supervise] entered supervision loop"
  local dead_streak=0
  while true; do
    sleep 30
    local judge_down=0
    local i
    for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
      if [[ -f "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" ]] && ! kill -0 "$(cat "$(judge_pidfile "$i")")" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "[supervise] ERROR: judge-$i died" >&2
        judge_down=1
      fi
    done
    if (( NUM_JUDGE > 1 )) && [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] \
       && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[supervise] ERROR: judge router died" >&2
      judge_down=1
    fi
    if (( judge_down )); then
      dead_streak=$(( dead_streak + 1 ))
      if (( dead_streak >= 2 )); then
        echo "[supervise] judge tier is down; aborting the run" >&2
        do_stop
        exit 1
      fi
    else
      dead_streak=0
    fi
    if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]] && [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] \
       && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[supervise] WARNING: probe died — uncertain verdicts will be dropped" >&2
      if [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]]; then do_stop; exit 1; fi
    fi
  done
}

do_logs() {
  case "${LOGSEL}" in
    probe)  tail -n 200 -f "${PROBE_LOG}" ;;
    router) tail -n 200 -f "${ROUTER_LOG}" ;;
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") logs [0-$((NUM_JUDGE-1))|router|probe]" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *)      tail -n 200 -f "$(judge_log "${LOGSEL}")" ;;
  esac
}

case "${ACTION}" in
  start)  do_start ;;
  stop)   do_stop ;;
  restart) do_stop; sleep 3; do_start ;;
  supervise) do_supervise ;;
  status) do_status ;;
  logs)   do_logs ;;
  *) usage; exit 1 ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GUI Actor RL — reward services (frozen judge replicas + holo3 probe) on dedicated GPUs.
#
# Started from the *worker* rank of the training job, after Ray and the env workers,
# on the GPUs that are NOT handed to Ray. It brings up:
#
#   judge-0..N-1   sglang, tp=1 each, one GPU each   ─┐
#                                                     ├─ sglang_router → JUDGE_PORT
#   probe          holo3 35B-A3B, tp=PROBE_TP          (exposed on PROBE_PORT, used directly)
#
# On success it writes ${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/reward_services.env with
#
#   GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://host_0:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1
#   GUI_JUDGE_MODEL_NAME=...
#   GUI_PROBE_BASE_URL=http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}/v1
#   GUI_PROBE_MODEL_NAME=...
#   GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=true|false
#
# Usage:
#   start_reward_services.sh start|stop|status|logs [worker-index|router|probe]
#
# Everything is env-overridable; see the config block below.

set -euo pipefail

ACTION="${1:-start}"
LOGSEL="${2:-}"

PYTHON_BIN="${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}"
REWARD_LOG_DIR="${REWARD_LOG_DIR:-/tmp/gui_reward_services}"
# Host written into reward_services.env. Set to the node IP when the trainer runs
# on a different rank than the services (host_0 only works same-pod).
REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST="${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST:-host_0}"
mkdir -p "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}"

# ── judge ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGE_MODEL_PATH="${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH:-${JUDGE_HF_CHECKPOINT:-/workspace/assets/judge-checkpoint/rollout_17}}"
JUDGE_SERVED_NAME="${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME:-guirl-judge}"
# ";"-separated GPU ids, one replica per entry (tp=1)
JUDGE_GPU_LIST="${JUDGE_GPU_LIST:-4;5}"
JUDGE_WORKER_PORT="${JUDGE_WORKER_PORT:-31101}"   # first worker; +i per replica
JUDGE_PORT="${JUDGE_PORT:-31100}"                 # router
JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION="${JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION:-0.60}"
JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT="${JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT:-1800}"
JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY="${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY:-round_robin}"

# ── probe (holo3 35B-A3B) ──────────────────────────────────────────
PROBE_ENABLE="${PROBE_ENABLE:-1}"
PROBE_MODEL_PATH="${PROBE_MODEL_PATH:-/workspace/local/models/Holo-3.1-35B-A3B}"
PROBE_SERVED_NAME="${PROBE_SERVED_NAME:-holo3-1-35b-a3b}"
PROBE_GPUS="${PROBE_GPUS:-6,7}"                   # comma-separated, tp=PROBE_TP
PROBE_TP="${PROBE_TP:-2}"
PROBE_PORT="${PROBE_PORT:-31200}"
PROBE_BACKEND="${PROBE_BACKEND:-sglang}"          # sglang | vllm
PROBE_MEM_FRACTION="${PROBE_MEM_FRACTION:-0.65}"
# Mirrors external/pkgs/run_agentplat/scripts/start_holo31_35b_sglang.sh (the known-good
# Holo-3.1-35B-A3B recipe): qwen3 reasoning parser keeps <think> out of `content`, which
# the probe's JSON-schema parser depends on.
PROBE_REASONING_PARSER="${PROBE_REASONING_PARSER:-qwen3}"
PROBE_DTYPE="${PROBE_DTYPE:-bfloat16}"
PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS="${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS:-64}"
PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND="${PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND:-flashinfer}"
PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT="${PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT:-3600}"

PROBE_REQUIRED="${PROBE_REQUIRED:-0}"

export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="${PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF:-expandable_segments:True}"

IFS=';' read -r -a JUDGE_GPUS <<< "${JUDGE_GPU_LIST}"

judge_pidfile() { echo "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-$1.pid"; }

usage() {

wait_http() {  # url, pidfile, timeout_s, label, log
  local url="$1" pidfile="$2" timeout="$3" label="$4" log="$5"
  local deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + timeout ))
  printf '[%s] waiting for %s ' "${label}" "${url}"
  while true; do
    if curl -sf "${url}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo " ready"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]] && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${pidfile}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "[${label}] ERROR: process died — see ${log}" >&2
      tail -40 "${log}" >&2 || true
      return 1
    fi
    if (( $(date +%s) > deadline )); then
      echo ""
      echo "[${label}] ERROR: not ready within ${timeout}s — see ${log}" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    printf '.'
    sleep 5
  done

  echo "[judge-$i] starting — GPU ${gpu}, port ${port}"

    --model-path "${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}" \
    --served-model-name "${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}" \
    --host host_1 \
    --port "${port}" \
    --tp-size 1 \
    --mem-fraction-static "${JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION}" \
    > "${log}" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "${pidfile}"

start_probe() {
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" != "1" ]]; then
    echo "[probe] disabled (PROBE_ENABLE=${PROBE_ENABLE})"

  fi
  if [[ ! -d "${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" ]]; then

  fi
  if [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "[probe] already running (pid $(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")) on GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "[probe] starting — GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS} (tp=${PROBE_TP}), port ${PROBE_PORT}, backend ${PROBE_BACKEND}"
  case "${PROBE_BACKEND}" in
    sglang)
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${PROBE_GPUS}" "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang.launch_server \

        --served-model-name "${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}" \

        --served-model-name "${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${PROBE_PORT}" \
        --tensor-parallel-size "${PROBE_TP}" \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --dtype "${PROBE_DTYPE}" \
        --max-num-seqs "${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS}" \
        --reasoning-parser holo2 \
        > "${PROBE_LOG}" 2>&1 &

do_start() {

    echo "   probe : DISABLED"
  fi
  echo "============================================================"

=== start_reward_services.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GUI Actor RL — reward services (frozen judge replicas + holo3 probe) on dedicated GPUs.
#
# Started from the *worker* rank of the training job, after Ray and the env workers,
# on the GPUs that are NOT handed to Ray. It brings up:
#
#   judge-0..N-1   sglang, tp=1 each, one GPU each   ─┐
#                                                     ├─ sglang_router → JUDGE_PORT
#   probe          holo3 35B-A3B, tp=PROBE_TP          (exposed on PROBE_PORT, used directly)
#
# On success it writes ${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/reward_services.env with
#
#   GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://host_0:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1
#   GUI_JUDGE_MODEL_NAME=...
#   GUI_PROBE_BASE_URL=http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}/v1
#   GUI_PROBE_MODEL_NAME=...
#   GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=true|false
#
# Usage:
#   start_reward_services.sh start|stop|status|logs [worker-index|router|probe]
#
# Everything is env-overridable; see the config block below.

set -euo pipefail

ACTION="${1:-start}"
LOGSEL="${2:-}"

PYTHON_BIN="${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}"
REWARD_LOG_DIR="${REWARD_LOG_DIR:-/tmp/gui_reward_services}"
# Host written into reward_services.env. Set to the node IP when the trainer runs
# on a different rank than the services (host_0 only works same-pod).
REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST="${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST:-host_0}"
mkdir -p "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}"

# ── judge ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
JUDGE_MODEL_PATH="${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH:-${JUDGE_HF_CHECKPOINT:-/workspace/assets/judge-checkpoint/rollout_17}}"
JUDGE_SERVED_NAME="${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME:-guirl-judge}"
# ";"-separated GPU ids, one replica per entry (tp=1)
JUDGE_GPU_LIST="${JUDGE_GPU_LIST:-4;5}"
JUDGE_WORKER_PORT="${JUDGE_WORKER_PORT:-31101}"   # first worker; +i per replica
JUDGE_PORT="${JUDGE_PORT:-31100}"                 # router
JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION="${JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION:-0.60}"
JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT="${JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT:-1800}"
JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY="${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY:-round_robin}"

# ── probe (holo3 35B-A3B) ──────────────────────────────────────────
PROBE_ENABLE="${PROBE_ENABLE:-1}"
PROBE_MODEL_PATH="${PROBE_MODEL_PATH:-/workspace/local/models/Holo-3.1-35B-A3B}"
PROBE_SERVED_NAME="${PROBE_SERVED_NAME:-holo3-1-35b-a3b}"
PROBE_GPUS="${PROBE_GPUS:-6,7}"                   # comma-separated, tp=PROBE_TP
PROBE_TP="${PROBE_TP:-2}"
PROBE_PORT="${PROBE_PORT:-31200}"
PROBE_BACKEND="${PROBE_BACKEND:-sglang}"          # sglang | vllm
PROBE_MEM_FRACTION="${PROBE_MEM_FRACTION:-0.65}"
# Mirrors external/pkgs/run_agentplat/scripts/start_holo31_35b_sglang.sh (the known-good
# Holo-3.1-35B-A3B recipe): qwen3 reasoning parser keeps <think> out of `content`, which
# the probe's JSON-schema parser depends on.
PROBE_REASONING_PARSER="${PROBE_REASONING_PARSER:-qwen3}"
PROBE_DTYPE="${PROBE_DTYPE:-bfloat16}"
PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS="${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS:-64}"
PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND="${PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND:-flashinfer}"
PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT="${PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT:-3600}"
# 1 = abort if the probe cannot start, 0 = warn and continue with probe disabled
PROBE_REQUIRED="${PROBE_REQUIRED:-0}"

# Keep the allocator from failing on fragmentation under multimodal prefill spikes.
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="${PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF:-expandable_segments:True}"

IFS=';' read -r -a JUDGE_GPUS <<< "${JUDGE_GPU_LIST}"
NUM_JUDGE=${#JUDGE_GPUS[@]}

judge_pidfile() { echo "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-$1.pid"; }
judge_log()     { echo "${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-$1.log"; }
judge_url()     { echo "http://host_0:$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT + $1 ))"; }
ROUTER_PIDFILE="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-router.pid"
ROUTER_LOG="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/judge-router.log"
PROBE_PIDFILE="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/probe.pid"
PROBE_LOG="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/probe.log"
ENVFILE="${REWARD_LOG_DIR}/reward_services.env"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") {start|supervise|stop|status|logs [N|router|probe]}

  start      bring the services up and return
  supervise  bring them up and stay in the foreground (the training launcher needs this)

Env overrides:
  JUDGE_MODEL_PATH=${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}
  JUDGE_GPU_LIST=${JUDGE_GPU_LIST}   (replicas=${NUM_JUDGE}, tp=1 each)
  JUDGE_PORT=${JUDGE_PORT} (router)  JUDGE_WORKER_PORT=${JUDGE_WORKER_PORT} (first worker)
  PROBE_ENABLE=${PROBE_ENABLE}  PROBE_MODEL_PATH=${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}
  PROBE_GPUS=${PROBE_GPUS}  PROBE_TP=${PROBE_TP}  PROBE_PORT=${PROBE_PORT}
  PROBE_BACKEND=${PROBE_BACKEND}  PROBE_REQUIRED=${PROBE_REQUIRED}
  REWARD_LOG_DIR=${REWARD_LOG_DIR}
EOF
}

wait_http() {  # url, pidfile, timeout_s, label, log
  local url="$1" pidfile="$2" timeout="$3" label="$4" log="$5"
  local deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + timeout ))
  printf '[%s] waiting for %s ' "${label}" "${url}"
  while true; do
    if curl -sf "${url}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo " ready"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]] && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${pidfile}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo ""
      echo "[${label}] ERROR: process died — see ${log}" >&2
      tail -40 "${log}" >&2 || true
      return 1
    fi
    if (( $(date +%s) > deadline )); then
      echo ""
      echo "[${label}] ERROR: not ready within ${timeout}s — see ${log}" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    printf '.'
    sleep 5
  done
}

start_judge_replica() {
  local i="$1" gpu="$2" port="$3"
  local pidfile; pidfile=$(judge_pidfile "$i")
  local log;     log=$(judge_log "$i")
  if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${pidfile}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "[judge-$i] already running (pid $(cat "${pidfile}")) on GPU ${gpu}:${port}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "[judge-$i] starting — GPU ${gpu}, port ${port}"
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${gpu}" "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path "${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}" \
    --served-model-name "${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}" \
    --host host_1 \
    --port "${port}" \
    --tp-size 1 \
    --mem-fraction-static "${JUDGE_MEM_FRACTION}" \
    > "${log}" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "${pidfile}"
}

start_probe() {
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" != "1" ]]; then
    echo "[probe] disabled (PROBE_ENABLE=${PROBE_ENABLE})"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ ! -d "${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" ]]; then
    echo "[probe] ERROR: model path missing: ${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" >&2
    [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]] && return 1
    PROBE_ENABLE=0
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "[probe] already running (pid $(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")) on GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS}"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "[probe] starting — GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS} (tp=${PROBE_TP}), port ${PROBE_PORT}, backend ${PROBE_BACKEND}"
  case "${PROBE_BACKEND}" in
    sglang)
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${PROBE_GPUS}" "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path "${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" \
        --served-model-name "${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${PROBE_PORT}" \
        --tp-size "${PROBE_TP}" \
        --mem-fraction-static "${PROBE_MEM_FRACTION}" \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --dtype "${PROBE_DTYPE}" \
        --max-running-requests "${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS}" \
        --attention-backend "${PROBE_ATTENTION_BACKEND}" \
        --reasoning-parser "${PROBE_REASONING_PARSER}" \
        > "${PROBE_LOG}" 2>&1 &
      ;;
    vllm)
      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${PROBE_GPUS}" "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
        --model "${PROBE_MODEL_PATH}" \
        --served-model-name "${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${PROBE_PORT}" \
        --tensor-parallel-size "${PROBE_TP}" \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --dtype "${PROBE_DTYPE}" \
        --max-num-seqs "${PROBE_MAX_RUNNING_REQUESTS}" \
        --reasoning-parser holo2 \
        > "${PROBE_LOG}" 2>&1 &
      ;;
    *)
      echo "[probe] ERROR: unknown PROBE_BACKEND=${PROBE_BACKEND}" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  echo $! > "${PROBE_PIDFILE}"
}

write_envfile() {
  local probe_enabled="false"
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]] && [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] \
     && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    probe_enabled="true"
  fi
  cat > "${ENVFILE}" <<EOF
# generated by start_reward_services.sh at $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
export GUI_REWARD_SOURCE=judge
export GUI_JUDGE_EXTERNAL=1
export GUI_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1
export GUI_JUDGE_MODEL_NAME=${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}
export GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=${probe_enabled}
export GUI_PROBE_BASE_URL=http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${PROBE_PORT}/v1
export GUI_PROBE_MODEL_NAME=${PROBE_SERVED_NAME}
EOF
  echo "wrote ${ENVFILE}"
  cat "${ENVFILE}"
}

do_start() {
  if [[ ! -d "${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: JUDGE_MODEL_PATH not found: ${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "=== reward services (judge replicas=${NUM_JUDGE}, probe=${PROBE_ENABLE}) ==="
  echo "  judge model:  ${JUDGE_MODEL_PATH}"
  echo "  probe model:  ${PROBE_MODEL_PATH} (tp=${PROBE_TP}, GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS})"

  local i gpu port
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
    gpu="${JUDGE_GPUS[$i]}"
    port=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT + i ))
    start_judge_replica "${i}" "${gpu}" "${port}"
  done

  # probe starts in the background; judge readiness is the critical path
  start_probe || { echo "[probe] failed to start" >&2; exit 1; }

  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
    wait_http "$(judge_url "$i")" "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" "${JUDGE_READY_TIMEOUT}" "judge-$i" "$(judge_log "$i")"
  done

  if (( NUM_JUDGE > 1 )); then
    if [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[router] already running (pid $(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}"))"
    else
      local worker_urls=()
      for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
        worker_urls+=("--worker-urls" "$(judge_url "$i")")
      done
      echo "[router] :${JUDGE_PORT} → ${NUM_JUDGE} workers (${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY})"
      "${PYTHON_BIN}" -m sglang_router.launch_router \
        "${worker_urls[@]}" \
        --host host_1 \
        --port "${JUDGE_PORT}" \
        --policy "${JUDGE_ROUTER_POLICY}" \
        > "${ROUTER_LOG}" 2>&1 &
      echo $! > "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}"
      wait_http "http://host_0:${JUDGE_PORT}" "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" 300 "router" "${ROUTER_LOG}"
    fi
  else
    echo "[router] single judge replica — exposing :${JUDGE_PORT} directly is unnecessary"
    # keep the contract stable: point the env file at the single worker port
    JUDGE_PORT=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT ))
  fi

  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    if wait_http "http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}" "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" "${PROBE_READY_TIMEOUT}" "probe" "${PROBE_LOG}"; then
      :
    else
      if [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]]; then
        echo "[probe] required but not ready — aborting" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "[probe] WARNING: probe not ready; continuing with GUI_PROBE_ENABLE=false" >&2
      PROBE_ENABLE=0
    fi
  fi

  write_envfile
  echo ""
  echo "============================================================"
  echo " reward services ready"
  echo "   judge : http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${JUDGE_PORT}/v1  (${JUDGE_SERVED_NAME}, ${NUM_JUDGE} replica(s))"
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    echo "   probe : http://${REWARD_PUBLIC_HOST}:${PROBE_PORT}/v1  (${PROBE_SERVED_NAME})"
  else
    echo "   probe : DISABLED"
  fi
  echo "============================================================"
}

kill_pidfile() {
  local pidfile="$1" label="$2"
  if [[ -f "${pidfile}" ]]; then
    local pid; pid=$(cat "${pidfile}")
    if kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "stopping ${label} (pid ${pid})"
      kill "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
      for _ in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 1; done
      kill -9 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    rm -f "${pidfile}"
  fi
}

do_stop() {
  local i
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do kill_pidfile "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" "judge-$i"; done
  kill_pidfile "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" "judge-router"
  kill_pidfile "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" "probe"
  rm -f "${ENVFILE}"
  echo "all reward services stopped"
}

do_status() {
  local i port
  for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
    port=$(( JUDGE_WORKER_PORT + i ))
    if [[ -f "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "$(judge_pidfile "$i")")" 2>/dev/null; then
      local h; h=$(curl -sf "http://host_0:${port}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo healthy || echo starting)
      echo "  judge-$i [GPU ${JUDGE_GPUS[$i]}]: running — :${port} (${h})"
    else
      echo "  judge-$i: NOT running"
    fi
  done
  if [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "  router: running — :${JUDGE_PORT}"
  else
    echo "  router: NOT running"
  fi
  if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]]; then
    if [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] && kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      local h; h=$(curl -sf "http://host_0:${PROBE_PORT}/health" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo healthy || echo starting)
      echo "  probe [GPUs ${PROBE_GPUS}]: running — :${PROBE_PORT} (${h})"
    else
      echo "  probe: NOT running"
    fi
  else
    echo "  probe: disabled"
  fi
}

# Stay in the foreground so the training launcher (which aborts on any non-trainer
# child exiting, even with rc=0) keeps us alive for the whole run.
do_supervise() {
  local rc=0
  do_start || rc=$?
  if (( rc != 0 )); then
    echo "[supervise] startup failed (rc=${rc}); not supervising" >&2
    exit "${rc}"
  fi
  trap 'echo "[supervise] stopping reward services"; do_stop; exit 0' TERM INT
  echo "[supervise] entered supervision loop"
  local dead_streak=0
  while true; do
    sleep 30
    local judge_down=0
    local i
    for (( i=0; i<NUM_JUDGE; i++ )); do
      if [[ -f "$(judge_pidfile "$i")" ]] && ! kill -0 "$(cat "$(judge_pidfile "$i")")" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "[supervise] ERROR: judge-$i died" >&2
        judge_down=1
      fi
    done
    if (( NUM_JUDGE > 1 )) && [[ -f "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}" ]] \
       && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${ROUTER_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[supervise] ERROR: judge router died" >&2
      judge_down=1
    fi
    if (( judge_down )); then
      dead_streak=$(( dead_streak + 1 ))
      if (( dead_streak >= 2 )); then
        echo "[supervise] judge tier is down; aborting the run" >&2
        do_stop
        exit 1
      fi
    else
      dead_streak=0
    fi
    if [[ "${PROBE_ENABLE}" == "1" ]] && [[ -f "${PROBE_PIDFILE}" ]] \
       && ! kill -0 "$(cat "${PROBE_PIDFILE}")" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "[supervise] WARNING: probe died — uncertain verdicts will be dropped" >&2
      if [[ "${PROBE_REQUIRED}" == "1" ]]; then do_stop; exit 1; fi
    fi
  done
}

do_logs() {
  case "${LOGSEL}" in
    probe)  tail -n 200 -f "${PROBE_LOG}" ;;
    router) tail -n 200 -f "${ROUTER_LOG}" ;;
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") logs [0-$((NUM_JUDGE-1))|router|probe]" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *)      tail -n 200 -f "$(judge_log "${LOGSEL}")" ;;
  esac
}

case "${ACTION}" in
  start)  do_start ;;
  stop)   do_stop ;;
  restart) do_stop; sleep 3; do_start ;;
  supervise) do_supervise ;;
  status) do_status ;;
  logs)   do_logs ;;
  *) usage; exit 1 ;;
esac

steps.message: Now let me quantify the judge-vs-env relationship in the recorded per-sample history, and read the exact judge reward mapping in the rollout code.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to trace why rollout 0 crashed and why DAPO accepted only 7/32 groups. I start from the numbers: 73 of 96 groups are rejected as "inconsistent_reward", 3 as low std, 13 as invalid episodes, leaving 7 accepted. The suspicion is that `candidate_reward_mean` and `full_success_rate` both equal 0.65 while all candidate rewards are binary 0/1.

I check the audit in `dapo.episode_rewards`: it reads `score = float(child.get_reward_value(args))` and `env_score = float(child.metadata['gui_score'])`, then returns None with 'inconsistent_reward' when `abs(score - env_score) > 1e-6`. In judge mode `score` is the judge verdict (1.0 success, 0.0 failure), while `env_score` is the rule-based `gui_score` kept only for monitoring. The task history confirms the disagreement: env_score=1.0 with judge_status=failure and reward_score=0.0. So any episode where the judge differs from the rule-based check rejects its whole group. With 65% env success against frequent judge failures, 73/96 rejections follow directly.

The per-child check `max(values) - min(values) > 1e-9` is not the culprit, since children of one trajectory share a reward. The run also submitted the full budget of 96 groups and finished at 4015s, well under the 6000s timeout, so slowness is not the crash cause. The root cause is the equality check between two different reward sources.

arguments.command:
cd /user/user1/autorlbench-runs/20261114162314-005c3b/workspace
python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import json,collections,statistics
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open('observed_run/logs/rollout_timing/task_history.jsonl')]
print("n samples",len(rows),"groups",len({r['group_index'] for r in rows}))
print("judge_status",collections.Counter(r['judge_status'] for r in rows))
print("status",collections.Counter(r['status'] for r in rows))
print("removed",collections.Counter(r['removed_from_training'] for r in rows))
agree=collections.Counter()
for r in rows:
    agree[(round(r['env_score'],2), r['reward_score'] if r['judge_status']!='uncertain' else 'unc')]+=1
print("env vs judge reward:")
for k,v in sorted(agree.items(), key=lambda x:-x[1]): print("  env=%s judge_reward=%s n=%d"%(k[0],k[1],v))
# disagreement when both defined
d=[r for r in rows if r['judge_status'] in ('success','failure')]
mis=[r for r in d if abs(r['reward_score']-r['env_score'])>1e-6]
print("defined verdicts",len(d),"judge!=env",len(mis), "rate",len(mis)/len(d))
# per group: how many groups would be fully consistent judge==env and nonzero std
g=collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows: g[r['group_index']].append(r)
ok=0; bad=0; lowstd=0; unc=0
for gi,rs in g.items():
    if any(r['judge_status']=='uncertain' or r['removed_from_training'] for r in rs): unc+=1; continue
    if any(abs(r['reward_score']-r['env_score'])>1e-6 for r in rs): bad+=1; continue
    vals=[r['reward_score'] for r in rs]
    if statistics.stdev(vals)<=1e-6: lowstd+=1
    else: ok+=1
print("groups: ok=%d inconsistent=%d lowstd=%d uncertain/dropped=%d"%(ok,bad,lowstd,unc))
# within-group reward variation among defined samples
vars_=[len({r['reward_score'] for r in rs}) for rs in g.values()]
print("groups with >1 distinct reward:",sum(1 for v in vars_ if v>1),"of",len(g))
EOF

The `episode_rewards` path requires `score == gui_score` within 1e-6, otherwise 'inconsistent_reward'. I observe 292/716 defined verdicts disagree (41%), with 55-73 of 96 groups rejected for inconsistent_reward and 7/32 accepted before a RuntimeError. Removing the judge==env equality check, 82/96 groups still have more than 1 distinct reward, so that check is the dominant killer. steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to reconcile the audit's rejection tallies with my own per-sample recomputation and settle the diagnosis of why the run rejected 89 of 96 groups. I group task_history's 768 rows (96 groups of 8) and get 45 groups with any judge-vs-env inconsistency, 31 with any dropped or aborted sample, and 13 with zero variance, plus 7 clean groups: 45+31+13+7 = 96. The audit instead reports 73 rejected_inconsistent_reward, 13 invalid_episode, 3 zero_or_low_std, 7 accepted. The difference is precedence: episode_rewards returns the first error per child, so an inconsistent reward masks the aborted child behind it, and most dropped-sample groups get attributed to the equality check rather than to invalid_episode. Both tallies describe the same defect set.

Removing the judge-vs-env equality check leaves the groups with no dropped sample (96-31 = 65), minus the 13 zero-std groups: 52 of 96 groups qualify, well above the 32 needed for a batch. The check is a leftover from env-reward mode and is incompatible with judge mode, where score is the judge verdict and gui_score is the env outcome.

Independently, 292 of 716 defined verdicts (40.8%) disagree with the env: the judge calls failure on 33 env=1.0 samples and success on 60 env=0.0 samples. Judge latency consumes 1094s of 1713s (97%), and 49 of 768 samples abort on the 2000s timeout (6.4%); 291 of 768 (37.9%) are truncated, which the filter permits.

The router starts with a single worker URL, http://host_0:31102, though two replicas launch on 31101 and 31102, so throughput is halved and timeouts are likelier. The crash occurs at rollout 0, before any checkpoint is saved and before any evaluation runs, so no held-out evidence exists for this run.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /logs/artifacts && cat > /logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md <<'EOF'
# Verdict: UNHEALTHY — the run never completed a single training rollout

Rollout 0 aborted with `RuntimeError: DAPO exhausted 96 candidate groups: accepted 7/32;
refusing a partial update` and the job exited non-zero. No optimizer step, no checkpoint,
and no held-out evaluation ever ran.

## Root cause: the DAPO filter rejects any group whose judge reward disagrees with the env score

In this run `gui_reward_source: "judge"`, so `generate_with_gui.py` sets
`sample.reward["score"]` to the frozen judge's verdict and keeps the rule-based
environment score in `metadata["gui_score"]` / key `acc` "purely for monitoring"
(`generate_with_gui.py:14`, `_judge_reward` at ~461–479).

The dynamic-sampling filter does the opposite of monitoring. `dapo.py:episode_rewards`
requires, for every child episode:

```python
score = float(child.get_reward_value(args))        # judge verdict
env_score = float(child.metadata['gui_score'])     # env evaluate()
...
if abs(score - env_score) > 1e-6:
    return None, 'inconsistent_reward', None
```

That equality holds only in `gui_reward_source=env` mode, where `score` is defined as
`eval_score`. Under the judge it demands judge verdict == env verdict on every episode.

They disagree constantly. Across the 768 recorded episodes
(`logs/rollout_timing/task_history.jsonl`), 292 of 716 episodes with a definite verdict
(40.8%) have judge reward != env score. Example rows: 60 episodes with `env_score=0.0`
and judge `success`; 33 with `env_score=1.0` and judge `failure`; also all the partial
scores (env 0.5–0.9) that the binary judge maps to one extreme.

Consequence in the audit (`logs/rollout_timing/rollout_0000_dapo.json`):

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| groups examined | 96 |
| groups accepted | 7 |
| rejected_inconsistent_reward | 73 |
| rejected_invalid_episode | 13 |
| rejected_zero_or_low_std | 3 |

`inconsistent_reward` alone kills 73 of 96 candidate groups. This is the concrete root
cause; the "zero/low std" rejection that DAPO is meant to perform accounts for only 3.

This is not a variance problem hiding behind the label. 82 of 96 groups contain more than
one distinct reward, and the accepted groups have `accepted_std_mean=0.439`. Recomputing
from the per-sample history: if the judge-vs-env equality check were absent, 52 of 96
groups would qualify (96 minus 31 groups containing a dropped episode, minus 13
zero-variance groups) — comfortably above the 32-group target. The equality check alone
compresses 52 usable groups into 7.

## Symptoms, and what is not causal

- **Partial-update refusal is a symptom, not the defect.** `dapo_scheduler.py:176` raises
  because only 7 groups qualified within the 96-group budget. The budget itself was
  generous (3x `rollout_batch_size`) and it was fully consumed (`groups_submitted=96`).
- **Truncation is not causal.** 291 of 768 episodes (37.9%) terminated by
  `repetitive_action`/`max_steps`, and the filter accepts `TRUNCATED` status, so these
  pass. They lower reward quality, not acceptance.
- **Timeouts are a secondary contributor.** `gui_trajectory_timeout_s: 2000` dropped 49
  episodes (6.4%) as aborted, and judge latency dominates wall clock: e.g. sample 608 spent
  1094 s of 1713 s in the judge, sample 761 spent 1190 s of 1766 s. That inflates
  `invalid_episode` (13 groups) and drove `total_s=4015` of a 6000 s batch deadline, but
  removing it would not rescue the batch while the equality check stands.
- **Reward plumbing is internally consistent.** `reward_func` passes the precomputed dict
